Ray Tintori, a filmmaker who was in a relationship with ex-“Saturday Night Live” star Heidi Gardner, has died at age 43, multiple outlets reported.

The New York City Office of the Chief Medical Examiner told TMZ the cause and manner of death are under investigation.

Gardner is privately grieving with family and friends, sources “with direct knowledge” told the show-business site.

Tintori directed music videos from such bands as Arcade Fire and MGMT and was the assistant director on the critically acclaimed movie “Beasts of the Southern Wild.”

He also made a cameo as a newsreel cameraman in “Marty Supreme” (2025) and shot footage that was used in the movie as well.

In a 2025 post that appears prominently on his Instagram page, Tintori shared a gallery of photos with Gardner and rhapsodized over her on the comic’s birthday.

“Prettier and more graceful than the moon and by far the coolest person I’ve ever met,” he wrote. “My favorite song in the world is you singing softly in my ear. My favorite color is the gold at the center of your eyes. I remember the first time we saw each other and how you laughed with your whole body the second our eyes met, and I immediately fell so fast. I’ve just been falling faster every day. You are the sexiest woman who ever lived.”

“I am your boy forever,” he concluded.

Gardner, known in part for her character “Every Boxer’s Girlfriend from Every Movie About Boxing Ever,” was among the high-profile departures from “Saturday Night Live” in 2025.

A Gardner rep did not immediately respond to a HuffPost request for comment.
